name: Cloetta AB
reason: Confectionery maker with 10y adjusted EPS CAGR of only 6.3% (SEK), 10y avg ROIC 6.0% and 2025 EBIT margin of 14.0% at the 100th pctile vs a 10.6% average; consensus FY2-FY3 +7.4%/+6.4% so no credible >=7% route and no specialness.

name: Peab AB
reason: Swedish contractor/housing developer whose EPS fell from SEK 10.19 (2020) to 4.70 (2025) on a ~4% EBIT margin; earnings are set by the construction and housing cycle with no moat.

name: Baltic Classifieds Group Plc
reason: Dominant Baltic online classifieds network (auto, real estate, jobs) with EBIT margin rising from 37.9% to 68.2%, EPS growing every year (EUR 0.05 in 2022 to 0.11 in 2025), FCF conversion 1.61x, net debt 0.6x and consensus FY2/FY3 +17.8%/+13.7%; pricing power from network effects supports >=7%, though the market is small and the record short.

name: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd.
reason: State-controlled oil and gas producer/refiner whose EPS (INR 12.93 in 2020 to 39.13 in 2023) is set by crude prices and government windfall-tax/subsidy policy; consensus FY2/FY3 -9.6%/-0.2%.

name: IRB Infrastructure Developers Ltd.
reason: Levered toll-road BOT developer with net debt/EBITDA 6.15x, 10y avg ROIC 4.6%, negative 10y FCF conversion (-1.29x) and EPS down from INR 1.21 (2018) to 0.94 (2025); a balance sheet and economics that fail the Buffett tests.

name: Vedanta Ltd.
reason: Diversified metals/oil miner whose EPS swings with commodity prices (INR 9.36 in 2021 to 2.12 in 2023) and whose promoter group has a complex, heavily levered holding structure; consensus FY2/FY3 -6.1%/-4.8%.

name: Mangalore Refinery & Petrochemicals Ltd.
reason: State-controlled refiner whose EPS swung from INR -15.40 (2019) to 22.30 (2023) to 0.30 (2024) on refining margins; 10y avg ROIC 6.4% and consensus FY2/FY3 -13.1%/-21.1%.

name: UPL Ltd.
reason: Generic agrochemical maker whose growth came from the levered Arysta acquisition (acquisitions 1.62x 10y FCF), with EPS collapsing from INR 50.33 (2021) to -17.07 (2023) in a destocking cycle and 10y avg ROIC 6.3%.

name: Vodafone Idea Ltd.
reason: Loss-making telecom with negative EPS every year since 2016 (INR -2.22 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA 9.9x, share count up 33.5%/yr and survival dependent on government AGR/spectrum relief.

name: Oil India Ltd.
reason: State-controlled oil and gas producer whose EPS (INR 41.87 in 2022 to 27.39 in 2025, -27%) is set by crude/gas prices and administered gas pricing; 10y FCF conversion 0.30x.

name: Tata Chemicals Ltd.
reason: Soda ash producer whose EPS fell from INR 101.76 (2022) to 3.26 (2025) with EBIT margin at the 9th pctile (4.1%), 10y avg ROIC 3.9% and net debt 3.8x; commodity-priced earnings.

name: NMDC Steel Ltd.
reason: Newly demerged state-owned integrated steel plant with losses in 2023-24 (EPS INR -8.10 in 2024), a first marginal profit in 2025 (EBIT margin 4.1%), 3-yr avg ROIC -30.6% and steel-price-driven earnings.

name: Afcons Infrastructure Ltd.
reason: Shapoorji Pallonji group EPC contractor with EPS down 48% in FY2025 (INR 6.84), ~7% EBIT margin, negative 10y FCF conversion (-1.21x) and earnings set by lumpy government tender flow.

name: National Aluminium Co. Ltd.
reason: State-owned alumina/aluminium producer at a cyclical peak: EBIT margin 40.6% (91st pctile vs 17.9% avg), EPS 1.0x its 10y max after rising from INR 0.71 (2019) to 31.79 (2025) on alumina prices; consensus FY2/FY3 +1.8%/+1.3%.

name: KEC International Ltd.
reason: Power-transmission/rail EPC contractor with ~7% EBIT margin, EPS falling from INR 22.10 (2019) to 7.52 (2022) on commodity cost overruns, negative 10y FCF conversion (-0.37x) and net debt 2.7x; no moat.

name: InterGlobe Aviation Ltd.
reason: IndiGo has a dominant low-cost position in a secular-growth market, but EPS swings violently (INR 205.63 in 2023 to -17.42 in 2025) on fuel, USD-denominated leases and grounding events, so 5-10 year earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Tata Steel Ltd.
reason: Commodity steelmaker with EPS ranging from INR 33.21 (2021) to 2.06 (2024), loss-making European operations, 10y avg ROIC 6.2% and net debt 2.4x; earnings set by steel spreads.

name: BLS International Services Ltd.
reason: Visa/consular outsourcing with EPS up from INR 1.22 (2020) to 16.65 (2025), ROIC 26% and net cash, but margin is at the 91st pctile after a sharp run-up, growth is partly acquired (acquisitions 0.43x FCF) and revenue depends on a few government contracts that can be lost or barred (MEA tender debarment in 2025).

name: Chennai Petroleum Corp. Ltd.
reason: IOC-controlled standalone refiner whose EPS swung from INR -139.5 (2019) to 237.3 (2022) to 11.7 (2024) on refining margins; earnings are set by crack spreads.

name: Knowledge Realty Trust
reason: Newly listed (2025) Indian office REIT with only a 4-year history, falling EPS (INR 10.29 in 2023 to 1.32 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA 4.5x and growth reliant on acquisitions (1.86x FCF); rent-roll economics with no evident >=7% organic route and no FFO actuals available.
